value: Announced at Autumn Budget 2024 (30 Oct 2024) and in a Treasury speech (11 Mar 2025); launched at Budget 2025 on 26 Nov 2025 with immediate effect. 15-30% of tax collected (excluding penalties and interest) when information leads to collection of at least £1.5 million; discretionary; anonymous reports are not paid. HMRC publishes only an annual total of all informant payments (£1.388 million in 2025-26, not split by scheme). Draft Finance Bill 2026-27 legislation (Jul 2026) would withhold 45% income tax from SRS rewards. OBR-certified costing forecasts extra yield of £10m in 2027-28 rising to £95m in 2029-30. No SRS payment reported yet.

value: HM Revenue & Customs makes discretionary payments to informants under section 26 of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005; the amount reflects tax recovered, revenue loss prevented and time saved, not a fixed share. HMRC's annual reports print the yearly total for 2018/19-2020/21 and 2023/24-2025/26 (£290,250 in 2018/19 to £1.388 million in 2025/26); other years come from FOI requests reported in the press or relayed by the Fisher review. HMRC does not publish the number or size of individual rewards. Complemented for large cases by the Strengthened Reward Scheme (gbr-hmrc-srs) from 26 Nov 2025.

value: Under the Law on the Protection of Whistleblowers (XIII-804, in force 1 Jan 2019, Art. 12) the Prosecutor General's Office may pay a one-off reward for valuable information. The law sets no maximum and no percentage: the reward is to be proportional to the damage caused or that could have been caused, and not tied to a court judgment; a commission of the Prosecutor General's Office sets the amount (Government Resolution 1133 of 14 Nov 2018). Requests and grants: 2019-2022 11 requests, 4 granted, EUR 34,000 (TI Lithuania); 2023: 3 requests, none granted; 2024: 3 requests, none granted (Prosecutor's Office activity reports).

value: Ontario's securities regulator pays 5-15% of monetary sanctions and voluntary payments of at least CAD 1 million, up to CAD 5 million; up to CAD 1.5 million is paid even if the OSC does not collect. Awards are discretionary; anonymous filing through a lawyer. The OSC announces individual awards by news release; its audited financial statements show payments to whistleblowers each fiscal year (to 31 March): CAD 7.5 million in 2018/19, then between nil and CAD 1.8 million a year; nil in 2025/26. No award news release between Oct 2024 and Oct 2026.

value: The Whistleblower Protection Office (Úrad na ochranu oznamovateľov) may grant a reward of up to 50 times the minimum wage for a qualified report once an indictment is filed or an administrative offence is finally decided; the reward is not a legal entitlement and depends on merit, lost earnings and assets protected or recovered. Fixed cap, not a share of money recovered. Annual reports 2021-2025 show 7 requests in total and no reward granted (2 still pending at end-2025). From 2015 the Ministry of Justice handled rewards under Act 307/2014 (svk-msr-rewards). launched = Office's first reward requests (Sept 2021).
